statement: Source dated 2024 reports: The assessment says floods and extended droughts affecting food security could exacerbate conflict and migration.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024 reports: The assessment says floods and extended droughts affecting food security could exacerbate conflict and migration.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 65, paragraph beginning 'Similarly, intense floods'.

uncertainty: Conditional national risk statement, not a measured climate effect on conflict or migration.

statement: Source dated 2024 reports: Dry Corridor drought followed by intense rain disrupts planting and harvests; the assessment reports agricultural labor-income losses for 13% of rural households and particular exposure among subsistence farmers.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024 reports: Dry Corridor drought followed by intense rain disrupts planting and harvests; the assessment reports agricultural labor-income losses for 13% of rural households and particular exposure among subsistence farmers.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 65, paragraph beginning 'Extended periods of drought'.

uncertainty: The percentage is a dated cited estimate.

statement: Source dated 2024 reports: The assessment places 73% of districts in high-drought zones, concentrated in high-poverty Usulután, Ahuachapán, Cabañas and La Unión departments.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024 reports: The assessment places 73% of districts in high-drought zones, concentrated in high-poverty Usulután, Ahuachapán, Cabañas and La Unión departments.
uncertainty: Uses a 2012 FAO map and legacy boundaries.

statement: Source dated 2025 reports: The 2025 NDC says 88.7% of national territory faces disaster risk; Cabañas, Morazán and Ahuachapán have high vulnerability combining socioeconomic factors, weak basic-service access and environmental stress.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025 reports: The 2025 NDC says 88.7% of national territory faces disaster risk; Cabañas, Morazán and Ahuachapán have high vulnerability combining socioeconomic factors, weak basic-service access and environmental stress.
institutions: Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources
uncertainty: National NDC assessment; the passage does not disaggregate by municipality.

statement: Source dated 2025 reports: The NDC sets a 2030–2035 objective to strengthen adaptation, food security and community resilience to reduce environmental and climate-related migration, and proposes a data system on such movements.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025 reports: The NDC sets a 2030–2035 objective to strengthen adaptation, food security and community resilience to reduce environmental and climate-related migration, and proposes a data system on such movements.
affected_groups: people considering environmental or climate-related migration
institutions: Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources

source_refs.locator: PDF pp. 49–50, section 4.5.3 on human mobility.

uncertainty: This is a planned policy objective and information system, not an evaluated result.

statement: Source dated 2025 reports: The NDC describes an interagency mobility mechanism coordinated by Foreign Affairs and MARN, with agriculture, migration, housing and territorial-government bodies, intended to connect mobility, environment and climate agendas.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025 reports: The NDC describes an interagency mobility mechanism coordinated by Foreign Affairs and MARN, with agriculture, migration, housing and territorial-government bodies, intended to connect mobility, environment and climate agendas.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 25, National Coordination Mechanism on Human Mobility.

uncertainty: The NDC states the mechanism's purpose, not its effectiveness.

statement: Source dated 2019-11 reports: The 2019 case study describes Dry Corridor rural communities as vulnerable to climate impacts and gang-related conflict; during a severe drought, small-scale farmers lost most maize harvests while community cohesion was low.
compact_statement: Source dated 2019-11 reports: The 2019 case study describes Dry Corridor rural communities as vulnerable to climate impacts and gang-related conflict; during a severe drought, small-scale farmers lost most maize harvests while community cohesion was low.

source_refs.locator: One-based PDF p. 11 (printed ix), rural-community theory of change

uncertainty: This is qualitative 2019 program-context research, not a current national estimate.

statement: Source dated 2019-11 reports: The study reports that gang dynamics required WFP to negotiate program access and beneficiaries to obtain permission to participate; field visits included San Miguel, Uluazapa, Jiquilisco, Ozatlán, Usulután, Suchitoto, Agua Caliente and San Salvador.
compact_statement: Source dated 2019-11 reports: The study reports that gang dynamics required WFP to negotiate program access and beneficiaries to obtain permission to participate; field visits included San Miguel, Uluazapa, Jiquilisco, Ozatlán, Usulután, Suchitoto, Agua Caliente and San Salvador.

source_refs.locator: One-based PDF p. 12 (printed x), access; p. 15 (printed 1), field locations

uncertainty: Historical March 2019 programme access. The site list is fieldwork coverage, not proof every locality had the same access constraint; not a 2026 gang-control map.

statement: Source dated 2019-11 reports: The case study reports that WFP resilience activities brought landless agricultural day laborers and smallholders into communication with landowners and local government, with observed contributions to social cohesion and women's empowerment.
compact_statement: Source dated 2019-11 reports: The case study reports that WFP resilience activities brought landless agricultural day laborers and smallholders into communication with landowners and local government, with observed contributions to social cohesion and women's empowerment.

source_refs.locator: One-based PDF p. 11 (printed ix), rural-community theory of change

uncertainty: Programme-specific qualitative observations from 2019; no counterfactual estimate or demonstrated national violence reduction.

statement: Source dated 2018-02 reports: The assessment ranks San Salvador, Soyapango, Ilopango and Cuscatancingo as most vulnerable to heavy-rain flooding and landslides; San Salvador recorded 209 floods and 79 landslides during 1960–2015.
compact_statement: Source dated 2018-02 reports: The assessment ranks San Salvador, Soyapango, Ilopango and Cuscatancingo as most vulnerable to heavy-rain flooding and landslides; San Salvador recorded 209 floods and 79 landslides during 1960–2015.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 63, discussion of the historical flood and landslide record.

uncertainty: Historical counts are not current risk rates.

statement: Source dated 2018-02 reports: During three years of rainfall anomalies, maize and sorghum yields fell 43% and bean yields 29% in La Unión and Morazán; over 90% of producers used maize-bean-sorghum systems.
compact_statement: Source dated 2018-02 reports: During three years of rainfall anomalies, maize and sorghum yields fell 43% and bean yields 29% in La Unión and Morazán; over 90% of producers used maize-bean-sorghum systems.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 90, Eastern Dry Corridor agricultural vulnerability analysis.

uncertainty: The report cites 2013–2016 yield figures; not current estimates.

statement: Source dated 2018-02 reports: Municipalities with more land in staple grains tend to have higher climate vulnerability, while adaptive capacity is very low across the studied Eastern Dry Corridor municipalities.
compact_statement: Source dated 2018-02 reports: Municipalities with more land in staple grains tend to have higher climate vulnerability, while adaptive capacity is very low across the studied Eastern Dry Corridor municipalities.
